subject: Discovery recap & next steps — reliability / graceful degradation (Synapse Financial)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleanor Brooks <eleanor.brooks@synapsefin.com>, Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv.m@synapsefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — reliability / graceful degradation (Synapse Financial)

Hi Eleanor / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap so we all have the same view and a short list of next steps. Appreciate the candid description of the pain.

Key pain points you highlighted
- Spikes in inference tail-latency during end-of-month batch runs and marketing campaign peaks (last major spike: June 9 outage, ~45m impact to availability).
- No consistent fallback behavior today — traffic either hits primary model and fails or times out, which surfaces as partial content to users.
- Cost sensitivity: you need predictable unit economics for monthly budgeting; currently hard to forecast during spikes.

Current stack (from the call)
- Primary: internal hosted transformer (8B) running on single-region GPU pool.
- Logging: ELK stack for app logs; limited token-level tracing from model infra.
- No prefix caching; rolling deploys but no automatic model fallbacks.

What success looks like (your criteria)
- SLOs: 95th percentile token latency <= 250ms for interactive flows, 99th percentile handling plan for graceful degradation.
- Clear fallback strategy that keeps user-facing reads available (reduced quality acceptable during incidents).
- Predictable monthly cost with ability to cap burst traffic or route to cheaper quantized model variants.

Quick proposed next steps (we discussed these on the call)
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra+security (60–90m) — to map networking and logging needs.  
2) We’ll send an initial SLO/fallback matrix and a one-pager on graceful-deg patterns (attachment).  
3) Pilot proposal: 2-week trial on a dedicated pool + rule-based fallback to a quantized 4B variant; measure user impact and cost delta.
4) Security checklist exchange (SOC2 artifacts / network requirements).

Action owners and timeline
- Ben: send SLO matrix + one-pager (today) — attached.
- Rajiv: share a short architecture diagram and recent incident post-mortem (if possible) — requested by Aug 24.
- Monica: schedule the technical deep-dive with our infra SEs (propose next Wed/Thu).

Questions for you before the deep-dive
- Can you share the PM/owner who will sign off on SLO targets?
- Are there hard outage windows (regulatory batch windows) where latency tolerance is especially strict?

Attaching: SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (SLA/SLO proposals) and redwood-fallbacks-one-pager.pdf (patterns and tradeoffs).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once Monica confirms availability.

Best,
Ben

Redwood Inference

From: Eleanor Brooks <eleanor.brooks@synapsefin.com>

Cc: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv.m@synapsefin.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — reliability / graceful degradation (Synapse Financial)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Quick responses inline.

Pain / incidents
- Correct on June 9 — that was the worst recent event. We’re sharing the post-mortem with you separately; it cites a cache stampede + a single-region GPU pool saturation.

SLOs
- 95th <= 250ms is our target for core interactive flows, but leadership will accept a documented graceful-deg approach that keeps availability above 98% during incidents.

Fallback approach
- We like the idea of a quantized smaller model for fallbacks, but we need to understand expected quality delta (BLEU-like metrics or human evaluation) and how you measure regressions.

Security / procurement
- We’ll need SOC2 Type II, encrypt-at-rest details, and an initial legal NDAs/SLAs draft for procurement.

Next steps
- I’ll share the June 9 post-mortem and an architecture diagram by Monday (Aug 24).
- Please include a short note on the expected latency/cost impact for the proposed 4B fallback during pilot.

Thanks — and please loop in whoever will own economics on your side.

— Eleanor Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering | Synapse Financial
eleanor.brooks@synapsefin.com | +1 (617) 555-0133
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleanor Brooks <eleanor.brooks@synapsefin.com>
Cc: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv.m@synapsefin.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — reliability / graceful degradation (Synapse Financial)

Eleanor / Rajiv — great, appreciate the quick turnaround and the post-mortem when you can. Short update and attachments answering your asks.

What we attached / included
- SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx: proposed 95/99 latency tiers, availability targets, and suggested guardrails for graceful-deg (how we route, cache, and cap).
- redwood-fallbacks-one-pager.pdf: expected quality delta from 8B -> quantized 4B (we include evaluation excerpts and a baseline human-eval note).
- Cost note (in SLO sheet): estimate for pilot — expected +12–18% token cost under normal traffic, but burst protection reduces unbounded cost during incidents.

Answers to your specific asks
- Quality delta: for conversational summarization tests (internal bench), 4B quantized shows ~6–9% drop in ROUGE-like metrics; in human evals degradation is often not noticeable for short-form generation. We’ll provide the exact evaluation set for your review before pilot.
- Regression measurement: Redwood Optimize can run prompt-level evals each deploy; we recommend a small prompt set you own to gate quality before fallback is allowed.

Proposed pilot schedule
- Week 0: wire up logging + token-level tracing (our side + yours).
- Week 1: enable dedicated pool + routing rules to 4B fallback at 10% traffic for canary.
- Week 2: escalate fallback thresholds to handle peak windows and measure cost/quality.

Requested from Synapse (by EOD Wed Aug 26)
- Post-mortem doc and architecture diagram.
- PM/owner who will sign off on SLOs.

Internal note (Aditya / Monica)
- Please confirm SE availability for Wed/Thu next week — prefer Wed 10:00–11:30 PT. Aditya, will need your input on dedicated pool sizing and a preliminary pricing band for a 2-week pilot.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the SLO sheet — I’m free Wed afternoon PT.

Best,
Ben

Redwood Inference
